title: BrandMentions Alternatives for Budget Social Listening in 2026
summary: BrandMentions runs $79-$499/month but covers TikTok through captions only. Compare it to Brand24, Awario, Determ, and YouScan for budget listening in 2026.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** BrandMentions is a genuinely affordable, self-serve social listening tool — Starter plans run $79-$99/month, with a 7-day free trial ("no obligations, cancel anytime") — backed by real historical data depth for a small, bootstrapped vendor. But its own content marketing stops short of claiming speech-to-text or on-screen visual analysis, and it monitors TikTok and other video platforms through captions, hashtags, and tagged accounts only. That gap is shared by nearly every other budget-tier alternative — Brand24, Awario, Determ, and (until July 2025) Mention — with one partial exception in this comparison: YouScan, whose logo/image recognition is genuinely confirmed on video content, though its audio coverage runs on captions rather than true transcription. Syncly Social is the only vendor here built natively for both audio transcription and on-screen visual detection.


Search for "social listening under $100 a month" and BrandMentions shows up fast — Starter plans start at $79/month billed annually, and the 7-day trial comes with no obligations. That's a genuinely low bar to entry. What's harder to find is confirmation of what happens once your brand gets mentioned in a TikTok video instead of a tweet.


BrandMentions is a real, actively operating product — not a shuttered tool or a quiet rebrand story like some of its category peers. Founded in 2015 in Iași, Romania by Razvan Gavrilaș and bootstrapped without outside investment (Source:[Tracxn, 2026](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/brandmentions/__Mv_kNht5B6lrmiNqw2PwJLOtjd0dwM_WV6c-PhuOBHk) ), it still ships pricing updates, responds to reviews, and markets itself to "12,400+ brands & agencies" in 2026 (Source:[BrandMentions, 2026](https://brandmentions.com/) ). The honest complication is scale, not survival: its public documentation runs thinner than the larger players it competes against on price — and that thinness matters most on exactly the question budget-conscious teams are asking in 2026: can this tool actually see what's said out loud or shown on-screen in a video, or only what's typed into a caption?


This guide breaks down BrandMentions' current pricing against the alternatives teams actually compare it to, flags which still qualify as genuinely "budget self-serve" in 2026, and — the most useful, non-obvious finding here — separates the vendor with genuinely shipped image/logo recognition from the ones only claiming "TikTok coverage" on paper.


## Why Do Budget-Conscious Teams Look for BrandMentions Alternatives?


Budget-conscious teams look for BrandMentions alternatives for two reasons: to confirm a smaller, bootstrapped vendor's depth before committing budget, and to find a tool that actually analyzes video content instead of just the text and metadata around it.


On the first point, BrandMentions holds up better than its size would suggest. It monitors a genuinely broad set of channels — social networks (including TikTok), news sites, blogs, forums, and review platforms like Booking, TripAdvisor, Yelp, Google My Business, and the App Store (Source:[BrandMentions Help Center, 2026](https://help.brandmentions.com/en/articles/12587203-what-online-sources-does-brandmentions-monitor) ). Reviewer activity is current too: Capterra shows a 5.0 rating across 64 reviews, with the vendor still replying as recently as November 2025 (Source:[Capterra, 2026](https://www.capterra.com/p/235227/BrandMentions/) ). None of that reads like a company coasting on an old feature set — it reads like a small, SMB- and agency-focused vendor doing exactly what it says on the label.


The second reason is where evaluation gets more interesting. A growing share of brand conversation now happens inside spoken video and on-screen visuals rather than typed captions, and teams comparing "budget" tools in 2026 are increasingly asking a question none of these pricing pages answer directly: does this tool listen to what's actually said in a video, or only to what's hashtagged around it? For BrandMentions, and for most of the vendors it gets compared against, the honest answer is the latter.


## How Does BrandMentions Pricing Compare to Its Alternatives?


BrandMentions runs four published tiers with no quote-gating required to see a number: Starter at $99/month ($79/month billed annually), Pro at $299/month ($249 annually), Expert at $499/month ($399 annually, marketed as "Most Popular"), and Enterprise starting from $1,299/month ($1,099 annually) — all backed by a 7-day free trial ("Try free for 7 days — cancel anytime") (Source:[BrandMentions Pricing, 2026](https://brandmentions.com/pricing.php) ). Each tier scales on keyword count, mention volume, and historical lookback: Starter covers 5 keywords and 5,000 mentions with 3 months of history; Pro moves to 20 keywords, 30,000 mentions, and 6 months; Expert adds Boolean search and real-time updates across 50 keywords, 75,000 mentions, and a full 12 months; and Enterprise adds API access and custom limits (Source:[BrandMentions Pricing, 2026](https://brandmentions.com/pricing.php) ).


**Budget self-serve social listening** : A tool priced low enough, and structured simply enough, that a team can subscribe and configure it without a sales call — in 2026, the real entry point for this category clusters at $29-$99/month, with a second, more feature-complete tier at roughly $250-$500/month before most vendors shift to enterprise quote-gating.


BrandMentions' $79/month annual Starter price sits squarely inside that first band, alongside Awario's $29/month annual Starter plan — the cheapest self-serve entry in this whole comparison — and Determ's €99/month (about $107) Focus tier (Source:[Awario Pricing, 2026](https://awario.com/pricing) ; Source:[Determ Pricing, 2026](https://determ.com/pricing/) ). The second band includes BrandMentions' own Pro tier at $299/month alongside Brand24's Team plan ($299/month) and Determ's Expand tier (€299/month, about $323), with YouScan's Starter3 plan at $499/month sitting at the very top of that range.

One line item in that table is worth flagging on its own: **Mention discontinued its self-serve tiers in July 2025.** The Solo, Pro, and Pro Plus plans that used to make Mention a fixture of "budget social listening" round-ups no longer exist for new signups — the current Company Plan is quote-gated only, with third-party analysis pricing it around $599/month on an annual-only contract (Source:[checkthat.ai, 2026](https://checkthat.ai/brands/mention/pricing) ). Mention's own pricing page confirms the quote-only structure without publishing a number (Source:[Mention Pricing, 2026](https://mention.com/en/pricing) ). If you're comparing "budget" tools for 2026 based on an older round-up that still lists Mention's old self-serve plans, that comparison is out of date — it no longer belongs in this category at all.


## Which BrandMentions Alternatives Cover Video Content, Not Just Text?


Almost the entire budget tier — BrandMentions, Brand24, Awario, Determ, and Mention — monitors TikTok and other video platforms through captions, hashtags, and tagged accounts only, with no confirmed speech-to-text or on-screen visual analysis; YouScan is the closest exception at self-serve pricing, with genuinely confirmed logo/image recognition (though its audio side runs on captions, not true transcription), and Syncly Social is the only vendor here with both natively confirmed.


**Text/caption-only listening** : Monitoring that scans captions, hashtags, tagged accounts, and platform metadata for keyword matches — it can't hear what's actually said out loud in a video or recognize what's shown on-screen.


**Video-native listening** : Monitoring that processes the actual audio and visual content of a video — transcribing spoken words and detecting on-screen text, logos, or imagery — surfacing brand mentions even when the caption and hashtags never say your brand's name.


BrandMentions is unusually direct about which side of that line it falls on, and it's worth taking that at face value rather than reading it as a hidden gap. In its own blog post comparing TikTok listening tools, BrandMentions' content describes cross-channel listening tools — its own included — as covering "captions, comments, hashtags, sentiment, alerts, SOV, adjacent web and news," while flagging that they miss "pure speech or logo-only detection, confirm per vendor" (Source:[BrandMentions Blog, 2026](https://brandmentions.com/blog/track-brand-mentions-tiktok/) ). That's about as clear a first-party admission as this category gets: BrandMentions isn't claiming to hear or see inside video content.


The rest of the budget tier tells a similarly consistent story, just with less self-disclosure. Brand24 lists TikTok as a monitored source, but its feature descriptions center on keyword and mention-text matching, with no mention of speech-to-text or visual recognition anywhere in its marketing (Source:[Brand24 Pricing, 2026](https://brand24.com/pricing/) ). Awario doesn't track TikTok at any tier — Reddit, Instagram, X, Facebook, YouTube, Vimeo, and news/web are the full source list, a gap this pipeline's Awario alternatives coverage has confirmed separately (Source:[Awario Pricing, 2026](https://awario.com/pricing) ). Determ likewise tracks no TikTok or Reels on any plan, leaning instead into a news archive of more than 100 million sites plus broadcast monitoring — strong for PR teams, unsuited to video-first brands (Source:[Determ Pricing, 2026](https://determ.com/pricing/) ). Mention lists TikTok and "Video" as sources, but its product descriptions point to caption-based matching, not confirmed audio or visual analysis.


YouScan partially breaks that pattern — on the confirmed side. Its Visual Insights feature genuinely recognizes brand logos, objects, and scenes inside images and video frames, and YouScan's own TikTok listening guide credits that logo recognition with surfacing "up to 80% more mentions than text-only monitoring" (Source:[YouScan Blog, 2026](https://youscan.io/blog/tiktok-social-listening/) ). Its audio side is thinner than that framing implies, though: YouScan's Audio Monitoring is a paid add-on, not a default, and per YouScan's own help documentation it identifies mentions "using captions or/and subtitles" rather than transcribing spoken audio directly (Source:[YouScan Help Center, 2026](https://help.youscan.io/en/articles/7245614-audio-monitoring) ). Syncly Social was built differently from the start, with[audio transcription and on-screen visual detection](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) running natively across every tier rather than gated behind an add-on.


That gap is only getting more consequential. Health and beauty alone now accounts for 79.3% of TikTok Shop sales, generating more than $1.34 billion annually (Source:[BeautyMatter, 2025](https://beautymatter.com/articles/tiktok-live-and-the-rise-of-a-new-role-in-beauty) ) — a category where an increasing share of brand-relevant conversation happens in spoken video or on-screen visuals a caption-matching tool simply never registers.


## Which BrandMentions Alternative Fits a Budget-Conscious Team?


"Budget-conscious team" splits into at least two different buyers here: teams that want the lowest possible entry price for text-based brand monitoring, and teams that need real video and audio coverage and are willing to pay a bit more within the same self-serve tier to actually get it.


### 1. Syncly Social


[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social) is built for teams whose customers talk about them out loud or show them on-screen inside TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts — conversation that BrandMentions', Brand24's, Awario's, Determ's, and Mention's caption-based monitoring simply doesn't register. Audio transcription and on-screen text and logo detection run natively across every tier, not as a paid add-on, and the entry point is a genuine free trial rather than a sales-gated demo. It's the strongest fit for teams whose evaluation criteria include real[social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) coverage of video content specifically — the exact gap BrandMentions' own content marketing acknowledges it doesn't close.


### 2. Brand24


Brand24 is the closest like-for-like comparison to BrandMentions on real-time alerting and sentiment analysis, priced higher across the board: Individual runs roughly $199/month (annualized), Team $299, Pro $399, Business $599, and Enterprise from $1,499/year (Source:[Brand24 Pricing, 2026](https://brand24.com/pricing/) ). It lists TikTok as a covered source, matching BrandMentions' claim, but shares the same limitation — text and keyword matching, no confirmed speech-to-text or visual recognition. More on how it stacks up against other budget tools is in[this pipeline's Brand24 alternatives guide](https://syncly.app/blog/8-best-brand24-alternatives-for-teams-ready-to-cover-video-too) .


### 3. Awario


Awario is the cheapest self-serve entry point in this comparison at $29/month billed annually, undercutting even BrandMentions' own Starter tier, and it differentiates itself with a built-in sales-lead discovery feature that surfaces potential customers from social conversations (Source:[Awario Pricing, 2026](https://awario.com/pricing) ). The trade-off: Awario doesn't monitor TikTok at all, on any plan — a strong fit for budget-first teams tracking text-heavy platforms, a poor fit for anyone whose brand conversation lives on video. More detail is in[Syncly's Awario alternatives breakdown](https://syncly.app/blog/awario-alternatives-for-8-tools-compared-on-tiktok-coverage-pricing-and-reviews) .


### 4. Determ


Determ leans into PR and media monitoring rather than social-first brand tracking, with self-serve pricing from €99 to €499/month (roughly $107-$540) and a news archive covering more than 100 million sites plus broadcast monitoring (Source:[Determ Pricing, 2026](https://determ.com/pricing/) ). Like Awario, it doesn't track TikTok or Reels on any tier — a reasonable trade for PR-focused teams, a structural mismatch for video-first evaluation.[Syncly's Determ alternatives guide](https://syncly.app/blog/determ-alternatives-for-10-tools-compared-on-pricing-and-video-coverage) covers this positioning in more depth.


### 5. Mention


Mention is included here mainly as a warning: as of July 2025, it no longer qualifies as a budget self-serve tool. Its legacy Solo, Pro, and Pro Plus plans have been fully retired for new customers, replaced by a single Company Plan that's quote-gated and annual-contract-only, with third-party pricing analysis putting it around $599/month (Source:[checkthat.ai, 2026](https://checkthat.ai/brands/mention/pricing) ). It lists TikTok and "Video" as sources, but nothing in its current marketing confirms speech-to-text or visual analysis beyond caption matching. If an older round-up still recommends Mention as a budget option, that recommendation is out of date.


### 6. YouScan


YouScan is the standout here on the confirmed part of its pitch: genuine logo and image recognition inside video frames, not just captions. Its Starter3 plan runs $499/month billed annually — more than BrandMentions, Brand24, or Determ — with an Unlimited tier at quote-gated pricing for larger volumes (Source:[YouScan Pricing, 2026](https://youscan.io/pricing/) ). Worth flagging before assuming full parity with dedicated video-audio platforms: YouScan's Audio Monitoring is a paid add-on that surfaces mentions from captions and subtitles rather than transcribing spoken audio directly (Source:[YouScan Help Center, 2026](https://help.youscan.io/en/articles/7245614-audio-monitoring) ). For a team whose core requirement is real image/logo coverage rather than the absolute lowest price, this is the closest budget-adjacent match to what Syncly Social offers natively.


### 7. Meltwater (enterprise contrast)


Meltwater sits outside the budget tier entirely — quote-only pricing analysts estimate at roughly $15,000-$30,000/year for small teams up past $150,000 for enterprise deployments, with a median buyer paying $25,800/year (Source:[Vendr, 2026](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/meltwater) ). It's included as a contrast point, not a genuine budget alternative: Meltwater has already shipped real TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram video transcription through its TikTok Marketing Partners integration, proving video-native listening is achievable at enterprise scale — just priced well outside what "budget" means here.


## Key Takeaways


-


BrandMentions is a real, actively operating, bootstrapped vendor (founded 2015, Iași, Romania) with published self-serve pricing from $79-$99/month (Starter) up to $1,299/month (Enterprise) and a 7-day free trial ("no obligations, cancel anytime").


-


BrandMentions' own blog content admits its cross-channel monitoring, including TikTok, misses "pure speech or logo-only detection" — a first-party confirmation that it's text/caption-based, not video-native.


-


Real budget self-serve entry pricing in 2026 clusters at $29-$99/month (Awario, BrandMentions, Determ), with a second tier around $250-$500/month (Brand24, BrandMentions Pro, Determ, YouScan).


-


Mention no longer qualifies as a budget self-serve tool — it discontinued its legacy self-serve plans in July 2025 and now runs a single, quote-gated Company Plan around $599/month.


-


YouScan is the only self-serve vendor in this comparison with genuinely confirmed logo/image recognition inside video ($499/month) — but its audio coverage is a captions-based add-on, not true transcription. Syncly Social is the only vendor here with native audio transcription and on-screen visual detection built into every tier.


## The Verdict


BrandMentions isn't a cautionary tale — it's a small, honest vendor doing exactly what its pricing page and its own blog say it does: affordable, self-serve text and caption monitoring across a genuinely wide set of channels, backed by real historical data depth. The problem isn't BrandMentions specifically; it's that almost its entire price bracket — Brand24, Awario, Determ, and the now-defunct budget tier of Mention — shares the same caption-only ceiling on video content, at a moment when a growing share of brand conversation happens in spoken video and visuals none of them can see. If the lowest entry price is the only criterion, Awario's $29/month is hard to beat. If real logo and image recognition inside video matters more than shaving another $20 off the bill, YouScan is the closest self-serve option — just confirm its captions-based audio add-on before assuming full transcription. Syncly Social is built for teams that want both audio transcription and on-screen visual detection natively, without a pricing page that stops at "custom."
